title: Root normalization in derived-arrow coordinates
statement: For Chern data c at arbitrary coefficient diagrams, assume the positive target-normalization predicate ChernData.rootNormalized. Then its root-isomorphism adjunction transpose, followed by the canonical forgetful shift, single-complex and root-identification comparisons, equals the positive Kummer boundary shifted once followed by the inverse shift-addition comparison. All endpoints are the literal full-units and roots towers.

proof.text: For a short complex constructed from generic endpoint objects, inclusion, power and zero relation, name its positive boundary with literal endpoints and unfold target normalization. This gives the displayed four-factor equation before specializing the category. Apply this generic theorem to the actual Kummer arrows and recorded short exactness. The named boundary has those same literal endpoints, so the specialized equation is exactly the required one.

theorem chern_root_normalization_equation
    (T : Scheme.{u})
    (R A : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology T) CommRingCat.{u + 1})
    (φ : SemilinearSections.systemRing.{u + 1, u, u + 1} (Scheme.ProEt.topology T)
        (fun n ↦ R.obj (op n)) (fun n ↦ R.map (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ n)).op) ⟶
      SemilinearSections.systemRing.{u + 1, u, u + 1} (Scheme.ProEt.topology T)
        (fun n ↦ A.obj (op n)) (fun n ↦ A.map (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ n)).op))
    (c : ChernData l T R A φ)
    (h : c.rootNormalized l T R A φ) :
    (c.reduction.derivedAdjunction.homEquiv _ _) c.rootIso.hom ≫
      (c.reduction.forget.F.mapDerivedCategory.commShiftIso (2 : ℤ)).hom.app
        ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (Systems T R) 0).obj c.rootModule) ≫
      ((c.reduction.forget.F.mapDerivedCategorySingleFunctor 0).hom.app
        c.rootModule)⟦(2 : ℤ)⟧' ≫
      ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (Ab T) 0).map c.rootForget.hom)⟦(2 : ℤ)⟧' =
    c.kummer.boundary⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧' ≫
      (shiftFunctorAdd (DerivedCategory (Ab T)) (1 : ℤ) 1).inv.app
        ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (Ab T) 0).obj (roots l T))
